walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme D: Religion, Peace & Conflict — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme D: Religion, Peace & Conflict brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme D: Religion, Peace & Conflict.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.

mcqs.q: What does the teleological (design) argument claim?
options: Apparent purpose, order or complexity in the universe implies an intelligent designer — Paley's watchmaker analogy is the classic example.
The design argument proves God created the world in seven days.
The design argument proves evolution is false.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
